_doc: Conversation bank (js/systems/convos.js). who: k_<id> | arch:<type> | role:<senior role> | staff:<role> | type:<classmate|senior|junior|teacher|staff> | student. when: conditions (see convos.js). replies[]: say (what you say), npc (their answer), fx (rel/trust/rivalry/respect/crush, stats, money, clout, favour, rep{}, knowledge{}, path{}, note[], items{}, take{}). Personal (k_) conversations happen once; general ones can return after ~60 days.

convos.open: "{me}, you snore like generator. Like NEPA generator wey dey cough."

replies.say: 😂 "Na you dey snore! I hear you!"
replies.npc: "Lie. I sleep like angel. Angels no dey snore."
"No wahala. Na lullaby now. I no fit sleep without am again."

convos.open: "If you could carry one thing from home to this hostel, wetin you go carry?"

replies.npc: "Me na my mama's pot of stew. The whole pot."
"And watch am with which light? NEPA go laugh you."
{name} goes quiet. "…Yeah. Me too."

convos.open: "I hid two packs of biscuits inside my pillowcase. Promise you no go tell anybody."

replies.npc: "My person!" They pass you one biscuit. Loyalty has a price and it is one biscuit.
"Blackmail? From my own bunkmate?" They give you a biscuit anyway.

convos.open: "I don count am. Na 47 days till vacation. Forty. Seven."

replies.say: 📅 "Stop counting, e dey make am long"
replies.npc: "You're right. 46 and a half then."
"Misery loves company. Welcome."

convos.open: "Senior just collect my Strongman. The whole tin. I no even taste am."

replies.npc: {name} looks at you like you just saved their life. "I owe you one tin, I swear."
"Report? You want make them finish me?" They shake their head.
"Na so e be," {name} repeats sadly.

convos.open: "You think say we go still be friends when we reach SS3?"

replies.npc: "Ehen! Say am again so God hear."
"Then we go be friends till forever, because I no dey snore."

convos.open: "I wrote a letter to my mum but I'm scared to post it. It says I'm not okay."

replies.npc: "…Okay. Will you walk with me to the post box?" You go together.
They tear it up and write another one. It sounds fake, even to you.

convos.open: "Tonight na my birthday. Nobody know."

replies.say: 🎂 "Happy birthday! Na why you dey quiet?"
replies.npc: You sing "Happy birthday" under your breath after lights out. They laugh into their pillow.
"You don't have to—" They take it anyway, smiling.

convos.open: "Make we make secret handshake. Every best friend get one."

replies.npc: You practise it twelve times. It is perfect. It is ridiculous.
"We ARE small pikin, {me}." They're right.

convos.open: "Who you think fine pass for our class?"

replies.say: 🙊 "I no dey talk that kind thing"
replies.npc: "Coward." They grin.
"No way. You first." Neither of you says anything. You both laugh.

convos.open: "SS1 is coming. They say departments go scatter everybody."

replies.npc: "Deal. Even if I hate Physics."
"True. The bunk no dey change."

convos.open: "Point of correction: you wrote 'their' instead of 'there' in your note. I couldn't not say it."

replies.npc: "You're welcome." They do not detect sarcasm. Or they do and ignore it.
They take your whole notebook and return it in red ink. Every mistake. Every one.

convos.open: "What did you score in the Maths test? Just asking. Casually."

replies.npc: Their eye twitches. "We'll see in the exam."
"You don't REMEMBER your score?!" They look genuinely disturbed.
"…Do you want me to explain the questions you missed?"

convos.open: "My father says second position is first loser."

replies.npc: "It's fine. It's normal." It doesn't sound fine.
"You would." But they almost smile.

convos.open: "I have a timetable for my timetable. Do you want a copy?"

replies.npc: You get a colour-coded timetable. You follow it for two whole days. Personal record.
"Vibes will not pass WAEC." They walk away shaking their head.

convos.open: "Do you ever just… want to read something that isn't a textbook?"

replies.npc: "Mark of the Cobra? I've read it four times." For once you talk about something other than marks.
"I contain multitudes," they say stiffly.

convos.open: "I couldn't sleep. I kept solving simultaneous equations in my head."

replies.npc: "Thank you, I'm aware."
"I tried. I started calculating the sheep's average weight."

convos.open: "If you get A in Basic Science, I will personally buy you a Jolly Roll."

replies.npc: "I have already budgeted for it. Just in case." Respect.
"Don't be greedy. Greed affects concentration."

convos.open: "The library has a new Biology textbook. I got there first. Obviously."

replies.npc: They hesitate, then put it between you. You read in silence for an hour. It is weirdly nice.
"I will." They do.

convos.open: "Everyone thinks I don't have feelings because I'm always reading."

replies.npc: "…Thank you." They push their glasses up, very fast.
"That's… actually a good point."

convos.open: "BECE is in a few months. I made flashcards for every subject. 1,240 flashcards."

replies.npc: "Two hundred and forty. Don't forget the two hundred and forty."
You quiz each other for an hour. They get everything right. You get some right. Progress.

convos.open: "New student. You look like person wey get extra Strongman."

replies.npc: "Hmm. I go check myself." They don't, this time.
"Small pikin with sense." They take it and leave you alone for the day.

convos.open: "Wetin you dey look? You wan fight?"

replies.npc: "Pass then." You pass.

replies.say: 😐 "I dey look the tree behind you"
replies.npc: {nick} actually turns to look at the tree. "…Which tree?" You're already gone.

convos.open: "This school food na punishment. Who cook this beans, abeg?"

replies.npc: {nick} laughs — a real laugh. "You funny small."
"Bread? Where you see bread?" They look hungry, not mean, for once.

convos.open: "I repeated JSS1. You know that?"

replies.npc: "…Yeah. Many people." They look at you differently.
"Watch your mouth."

convos.open: "Thank you for that… reading thing. Nobody must know."

replies.npc: A tiny smile. "Correct answer."
"After lights out. Bring torch."

convos.open: "Na me read that whole notice board this morning. Alone. Every word."

replies.npc: "Shhh! …But yes." They look proud enough to burst.
"Small small. One notice board at a time."

convos.open: "You think say I be bad person?"

replies.npc: "Trying." They turn the word over. "Okay. I go try more."
"…Fair."

convos.open: "You still remember that day you snitch? Every day I remember."

replies.npc: A long silence. "Hmm. Okay."
"…That one too, sha."

convos.open: "Football after siesta. My team. You dey?"

replies.npc: You lose 4–1 but {nick} passes to you twice. That's basically friendship.
"Book book book. Okay."

convos.open: "Watch this — who am I?" He folds his arms, frowns and says, "SIT DOWN BEFORE I SIT YOU DOWN."

replies.npc: "CORRECT! Ten points to the comedian!"
"Ah, close, but the VP adds 'my friend' at the end." He does the VP too. Perfect.

convos.open: "I'm writing a Nollywood film. It's called 'Garri: The Revenge'. You want role?"

replies.npc: "Method actor! I respect it."
"The weevils. Obviously. Season two: 'Weevils Strike Back'."

convos.open: "If I get punished for laughing in class one more time, my knees go resign."

replies.npc: "Impossible. It's a medical condition."
He stares at you. "Genius. Pure genius."

convos.open: "Rate my impression of you. 1 to 10." He walks past, scratching his head, looking lost.

replies.say: 😤 "Zero! I no dey walk like that!"
replies.npc: "You do. Everybody agreed. We had a meeting."
"Thank you, thank you. I'm here all term."

convos.open: "Serious question. Do you think I could be a real comedian? Like, on TV?"

replies.say: 🌟 "You're already better than half of them"
replies.npc: He looks at you for a second like he's saving that sentence somewhere.

replies.say: 😂 "If you stop laughing at your own jokes"
replies.npc: "That's part of the art, sha." But he thinks about it.

convos.open: "My dad called. He said 'make your mama proud'. Then he laughed. Then he coughed for a long time."

replies.npc: "He's fine. He's fine." He makes a joke. It doesn't quite land.
"He's where I got it from."

convos.open: "I put salt in the prefects' tea. Just a little. For science."

replies.npc: "Science requires sacrifice."
"Senior Ngozi drank the whole cup and said 'mm, nice.' Science is confused."

convos.open: "Seatmate, I didn't read for the test. Help me with question 3 abeg."

replies.npc: "Fair. Pray for me." He prays loudly. Teacher looks up.
He copies. You both pass. You both feel weird about it.

convos.open: "Do you like Maths? Be honest."

replies.npc: Her whole face lights up. "Finally. Somebody normal."
"Maths doesn't hate anybody. Let me show you something." Ten minutes later, fractions make sense.

convos.open: "In my town, girls don't usually go to boarding school. My mother fought for me to be here."

replies.npc: "Yes." She says it like a promise.
"Money, tradition, fear. Mostly fear." She looks at her shoes.

convos.open: "Can you keep a secret? I solved the bonus question nobody solved. I didn't tell the teacher."

replies.npc: "Because then everybody looks at you." She shrugs. "I like being quiet."
"Maybe." She won't.

convos.open: "The Ramadan fast starts next week. Will you… sit with me at the evening meal sometimes?"

replies.npc: At sunset she breaks her fast with dates and offers you one. It is a quiet, lovely ten minutes.
"Okay," she says, and means it.

convos.open: "Why do people think girls can't be engineers?"

replies.npc: She laughs out loud for the first time all week.
"I will build a bridge and name it after you."

convos.open: "I made you a puzzle." She hands you a folded paper: a geometry riddle.

replies.npc: You get it in five minutes. She nods, impressed. "Not bad."
You solve it at 11 PM under a torch and tell her at breakfast. She grins.

convos.open: "My uncle wrote again. He keeps saying JSS3 is 'enough' for a girl."

replies.npc: "No. It isn't." She folds the letter very small.

replies.say: 📚 "Then we make your results too good to ignore"
replies.npc: "…Okay. Study with me tonight?"

convos.open: "Customer! Biro, ruler, eraser — package deal. ₦150."

replies.npc: "Pleasure doing business!" The ruler is slightly bent. Business is business.
"Window shopping is also welcome. Come back when you're rich."
"Commission na 10%. Welcome to the family."

convos.open: "You know how much water dey cost outside? And inside here na ₦50? We dey waste opportunity."

replies.npc: He explains a whole business plan involving buckets and a wheelbarrow. It's alarmingly good.
"Money no dey rest, so why I go rest?"

convos.open: "I lost money today. A senior 'borrowed' twenty Jolly Rolls."

replies.npc: "That's seniority," he sighs. "Different name, same thing."
"I wrote it. Under 'bad debt'. He's SS3, I go collect for heaven."

convos.open: "My mama sells pepper in Oba Market. Twelve hours a day. I'm not going back to that life."

replies.npc: "Legit." He nods slowly. "Legit is also money."
"Strongest woman for Benin." He smiles.

convos.open: "Rate my new slogan: 'Osas Provisions — We Get Am Before You Need Am'."

replies.npc: "I go put am for my receipt book."
"'Osas: We Get Am.'" He writes it down. "Better. You get eye for business."

convos.open: "Lend me ₦200. I go return ₦300 by Friday."

replies.npc: Friday comes. He returns ₦300 and a receipt.
"Smart. Never lend money. Na me teach you that one."

convos.open: "Your shirt is not tucked in. Rule 14."

replies.npc: "Thank you." She looks almost surprised you listened.
"Nobody. Rules are rules." Her voice wobbles a tiny bit.
She recites rules 15 to 22 without stopping. You're impressed despite yourself.

convos.open: "Do people… talk about me? You can tell me."

replies.npc: "…Okay." She nods many times. "Okay. Thank you."
"You're lying, but thank you for lying nicely."

convos.open: "I write things down because if I don't, I forget I'm not alone."

replies.npc: "Who sits where. Who's sad. Who didn't eat." She looks up. "You didn't eat yesterday."
"It's just a notebook." It isn't.

convos.open: "Rule question: is talking after lights out allowed if it's whispering?"

replies.npc: She thinks about it seriously. "…I will allow it." History.
"Exactly." She seems relieved somebody agrees.

convos.open: "My mother is a magistrate. She says fairness is the most important thing."

replies.npc: "Even when it makes people hate you?" You don't have a good answer.
She frowns, writes 'kindness?' in her notebook. Then underlines it.

convos.open: "Do you like my bag? It's from London. My dad sent it."

replies.npc: "I know." She smiles, but it fades fast. "He didn't send a letter. Just the bag."
"It's a very expensive just-a-bag."

convos.open: "I have too many provisions. Do you want some Crunchos? Don't make it weird."

replies.npc: "Whatever." She gives you two packs, not one.
"I'm not. I'm reducing my luggage." You both know.

convos.open: "Everybody wants to be my friend because of my things. Do you?"

replies.say: 🙂 "I want to be friends with Zara"
replies.npc: She studies your face like she's checking for fake. "…Okay."
She laughs, surprised. "At least you're honest."

convos.open: "My mum is in London. My dad is in Abuja. I'm in Sardauna House. Family."

replies.npc: She rolls her eyes, but she sits next to you at dinner.
"It's fine. I have a big room. Two big rooms."

convos.open: "Teach me how to wash my own clothes. Nobody can know."

replies.npc: She is terrible at it. She gets better. You laugh until the bucket tips over.
"Forget I asked." She is red for the rest of the day.

convos.open: "You know chemistry is just cooking with rules?"

replies.npc: He explains titration using pepper soup. You will never forget it.
"Exactly! And Mr. Okafor na head chef."

convos.open: "I'm not hungry." His stomach growls loudly.

replies.npc: "I go pay you back," he says. "You no need to," you say. He pays you back next week anyway.
He laughs. "My stomach is a liar."

convos.open: "My mama sells in Aba market. When I finish school, I go build her a shop with glass doors."

replies.npc: "With TWO air conditioners."
"I will." He says it quietly, like a fact.

convos.open: "Sorry, I can't contribute for the class party. I… forgot my money at home."

replies.npc: He can't look at you. "Thank you. Don't tell anybody."
"Okay." He comes. He helps set up every chair.

convos.open: "You think person can be poor and still be first in class?"

replies.npc: He actually smiles. "Second. Dera is always first."
"I go write that one on my wall."

convos.open: "Race me to the tap. Loser carries the winner's bucket."

replies.npc: You lose. Obviously. But you lose by less than anyone else ever has.
"Coward!" He races the wind instead. The wind also loses.

convos.open: "English comprehension is my enemy. Every passage na about some English village I never see."

replies.npc: You read a passage as a match commentary. He understands it perfectly. "GOAL! The main idea!"
"We suffer together."

convos.open: "One day I go play for Super Eagles. You go come watch?"

replies.npc: "I go point at you when I score."
"I go dash you ticket. VIP."

convos.open: "My papa says football is for people who don't want to work."

replies.npc: "Thank you! Tell my papa!"
"…Yeah. Both. Okay." He looks determined.

convos.open: "Inter-house practice. You dey run for our house?"

replies.npc: "Proper! I go train you myself. 5 AM."
"Champions no dey sleep." He sleeps through it himself.

convos.open: "Sister/Brother {me}! Have you prayed today?"

replies.npc: "Let's pray now!" She prays for your exams, your bucket and your future spouse. In that order.
"He does. That's why I'm worried." She laughs at her own joke.

convos.open: "I'm leading praise and worship on Sunday. Will you be in the choir?"

replies.npc: You sing. Off-key. She says it was beautiful. She is a very kind liar.
"God likes cracked voices too!"

convos.open: "Some people say I'm too much. Am I too much?"

replies.npc: She hugs you, which is very much, but okay.
"That's fair. I'll pray in a smaller voice." She does not.

convos.open: "Halima and I made peace. We're praying for the same exams now."

replies.npc: "Different prayers, same God of results!"
"He's not confused. He's multilingual."

convos.open: "Can I borrow your ruler? Mine broke."

replies.npc: They return it with a tiny drawing on the back — a little house with a flag. "Interest."
"My eternal gratitude." They smile. You give them the ruler.

convos.open: "Do you think buildings can be beautiful? Like, actually beautiful?"

replies.npc: "YES. It looks like a general's hat. I love it."
"Wrong." They say it nicely.

convos.open: "Everybody is staring at us. Somebody started a rumour."

replies.npc: "Already ignoring." They are blushing slightly.
"Let them talk," they repeat, smiling.

convos.open: "I'm drawing the school. Where should I start?"

replies.npc: "…That's actually poetic. Okay."
"The beans heart." They laugh and start anyway.

convos.open: "As class captain, I'm conducting a survey. What would make this class better?"

replies.npc: They write it down very seriously. "Noted. I will raise it at the meeting."
"…The list is for order." But they write it down too.
"Unrealistic but popular." They write it down.

convos.open: "I've been class captain for three weeks and I already have grey hair."

replies.npc: There is genuinely one grey hair. You both stare at it in silence.
"Am I? Thank you. Nobody says that."

convos.open: "Help me arrange the chairs for the PTA meeting? I'll owe you."

replies.npc: Two hours of chairs. They talk about becoming governor. You believe them.
"Fair. Prep first. Always."

convos.open: "Remember JSS1? You were so small. You used to cry when Senior shouted."

replies.npc: "We both cried. Let's agree we both cried."
"From bucket-carriers to bucket-owners."

convos.open: "I think I want to study Medicine. Is that stupid?"

replies.npc: "Dr. {name}." They say it twice, testing it. They like it.
"ONE time! In JSS2!" They're laughing.

convos.open: "Our juniors are so soft. In our time, we washed seniors' plates."

replies.npc: "I AM an old man. I have back pain from carrying buckets for five years."
"Never. I remember." They mean it.

convos.open: "When we graduate, promise we'll still call each other."

replies.npc: "Every week. Even when you're rich and famous."
"Over the phone? You'll hear it?"

convos.open: "I got a letter from my dad. He wants me to choose between his house and my mum's for holidays."

replies.npc: "…You're right. Thank you for always saying the right thing."
"Your mum will adopt me." "She already has."

convos.open: "We're not as close as before, are we?"

replies.npc: "Lunch tomorrow. Our old table. No excuses."
"Yeah." The word sits between you like a closed door.

convos.open: "I'm in Science class. You're in…?"

replies.npc: "Excellent. Competition continues." They seem genuinely happy.
"Pity. Who will I beat?"

convos.open: "Do you ever think about what happens if we fail WAEC?"

replies.npc: "Me too." For once, they don't pretend to be perfect.
"Statistically, someone will." But they relax a little.

convos.open: "I applied to a school in Canada. I haven't told my father."

replies.npc: "Thank you. You're… the first person I told."
"Because if I don't get in, I failed twice."

convos.open: "I just realised I've never been to a party. Like, a real one."

replies.npc: "Dancing? Me?" They come. They dance like a calculator. It's wonderful.
"That's what I tell myself."

convos.open: "Rival or friend — what are we?"

replies.npc: "Rival-friend. Frival. I'll allow it."
"Good. I need someone to chase."

convos.open: "SS1. Now juniors dey fear ME. E no sweet like I think."

replies.say: 🙂 "Then be the senior you wish you had"
replies.npc: "…Like Senior Chuka." They nod slowly.
"I go use am to collect Strongman." They're joking. Mostly.

convos.open: "I read a whole novel. Eze Goes to School. The whole thing."

replies.npc: "Shhh! …Thank you. I go read another one."
"Things go fall apart for my brain." But they borrow it.

convos.open: "One JSS1 boy dey cry for corridor. Me, I gave am my biscuit. Who I be?"

replies.npc: "Don't tell anybody. I get reputation."

replies.say: 😂 "Who are you and what did you do with Jide?"
replies.npc: "Same person. Better version."

convos.open: "We still dey vex each other? Na five years now."

replies.npc: "…Okay. I tire too." A handshake, finally.
"And you snitched." Back to square one.

convos.open: "I wrote a stand-up routine about boarding school. Twenty minutes. Can I test it on you?"

replies.npc: It's brilliant. The bit about the garri queue makes you cry laughing.
He does five minutes. You beg for the other fifteen.

convos.open: "Some days I don't feel funny. I just do the jokes so nobody asks."

replies.say: 🫂 "You don't have to be funny with me"
replies.npc: He goes quiet. "…Thank you, {me}."
"Not today. But maybe one day." That's enough.

convos.open: "I got into the drama club finals. I'm playing a king. A SERIOUS king."

replies.npc: He bows dramatically. "Rise, my loyal seatmate."

replies.say: 😂 "Can you be serious for two hours?"
replies.npc: "No. That's the challenge."

convos.open: "Science class. Further Maths. This is the happiest I have ever been."

replies.npc: "Proud nerd." She shows you a theorem like it's a photograph of a loved one.
"Torture is a strong word. It's… intense love."

convos.open: "The Olympiad committee wants me to train in Abuja for two weeks. Will you write to me?"

replies.npc: "Every day is too much. Every two days." She's smiling.
"Deal. I always do."

convos.open: "I think I want to be a professor. Teaching girls from towns like mine."

replies.npc: "Professor Halima Sani." She writes it on her rough sheet. Then underlines it twice.
"…With a big library. And no uncles allowed."

convos.open: "I don make ₦40,000 since JSS1. All saved. All legit… mostly."

replies.npc: "The JSS1 bucket incident was a learning experience."
"Chief Executive Osas." He likes that too much.

convos.open: "Business question: if you see person dey sell exam expo, wetin you go do?"

replies.npc: "…Yeah." He looks away. "Just asking."
He laughs nervously. "Ehen. Exactly what I thought."

convos.open: "My mama called. Her blood pressure is high. I sent her everything I had."

replies.npc: "I'm lucky to have her." He wipes his face quickly.
"I can't take this." He takes it. "I'll return it twice." He does.

convos.open: "I'm thinking of becoming a lawyer. Is that too obvious?"

replies.npc: "Obvious is efficient." She smiles.
She laughs. "Five years of case notes."

convos.open: "I stopped carrying my notebook. Do I look naked?"

replies.npc: "…Free." She tries the word. "I like that."
"Under my mattress. Retirement."

convos.open: "Daddy's case is in the newspapers again. Everybody's whispering."

replies.npc: She grips your sleeve for a second. "I know."
"…I don't know. I don't know anything about him." She looks very young.

convos.open: "I want to start a charity. For kids whose parents are… busy."

replies.npc: "Really? Okay. Vice President {me}." She means it.
"Like me? That's… nice."

convos.open: "I learned to cook jollof. From your mum, over the phone. Don't laugh."

replies.npc: "Mostly." She brings you some. It is, in fact, mostly edible.
"She calls me 'my other daughter'." Zara looks like she might cry.

convos.open: "Scholarship renewal next week. I need top five again."

replies.npc: "Every night till Friday?" Every night till Friday.
"Always is a scary word."

convos.open: "I made a water filter from sand and charcoal in the lab. It works!"

replies.npc: He shows you. The water is cleaner than the tap's. Mr. Okafor gives him extra marks.
"A genius who still eats garri for dinner." He grins.

convos.open: "When I build my mama's shop, you'll cut the ribbon."

replies.npc: "The biggest scissors in Aba."
"Honoured is the right word." He shakes your hand formally.

convos.open: "The academy scout came back. He asked for my WAEC results AND my 100m time."

replies.npc: "English is still 50-50." He's nervous for the first time.
"Coach {me}." He actually shows up.

convos.open: "My papa came to watch inter-house sports. He saw me win. He didn't say anything. But he stayed."

replies.npc: "…Yeah. I think so too."
"Maybe. He bought me suya after." A big deal.

convos.open: "I've been praying more quietly lately."

replies.npc: "My brother wrote again. I just… listen more now." She smiles a small, real smile.
She laughs. "Rude. But fair."

convos.open: "Fellowship president election. Should I run?"

replies.npc: "Born for it? Or born again for it?" She laughs at her own joke for a full minute.

replies.say: 🤔 "Only if you'll still listen to people"
replies.npc: "…That's good advice. I'll write it in my Bible."

convos.open: "I designed a new hostel. Fans that work. Showers that work. Imagine."

replies.npc: "The {me} Wing. Okay. You'll have to sponsor it."
They show you the sketch. It's really, really good.

convos.open: "Everyone keeps asking if we're… you know. Together."

replies.npc: "I tell them to mind their business." They smile. "Was that right?"
"Mystery is good for our reputation."

convos.open: "My parents want me to study Medicine. I want Architecture."

replies.npc: "…They've never seen it." They look terrified and hopeful.
"Safe isn't the same as happy." They look away.

convos.open: "Senior Prefect nominations. My name is on the list. My heart is doing gymnastics."

replies.npc: "Have I? I hope so." They straighten their tie four times.
"It has already tripled."

convos.open: "I learned something: you can't make everyone happy. Even with a list."

replies.npc: "That's exhaustion. But okay."
"…I'll laminate it instead. But I'll be gentler."

convos.open: "Please, how do you say 'I am hungry' in a polite way? Here they say 'I wan chop'."

replies.npc: "'I wan chop.'" He practices. The whole dining hall cheers when he uses it.
"Mama, abeg!" Mama Iyabo gives him extra rice. He is amazed.

convos.open: "In Sokoto, the sky at night is full of stars. Here, the generator is louder than the stars."

replies.npc: He talks for an hour about camels, his grandmother and his father's farm. You both forget the time.
The lights go off at 9. You both look up. He's right — stars.

convos.open: "Your English is so fast. Can you speak slowly for me?"

replies.npc: "Thank you." He catches every word. He thanks you again, slowly, for effect.
"Wahala." He says it perfectly. "This word is very useful here."

convos.open: "I fixed the radio in our dormitory. It only needed one wire."

replies.npc: "Not yet engineer. Engineer-in-training."
He shows you. You understand nothing. He is very patient.

convos.open: "My English teacher said my essay was the best in class. Mine!"

replies.npc: "You told me." He beams.
It's about Sokoto at night. It's beautiful.

convos.open: "Sallah is coming. My mother is sending kilishi. You will taste."

replies.npc: The kilishi arrives. It is the best thing you have ever eaten.
He grins. "Your Hausa is improving!"

convos.open: "Why does everyone call me 'London'? I'm from Ogun State. Originally."

replies.npc: "It's FADING." It is not fading.
"…Okay, it is kind of fun."

convos.open: "In London we had Wi-Fi. Here we have… Mallam Musa's radio."

replies.npc: "…The Hausa news is honestly quite relaxing."
"Thanks. I think."

convos.open: "I made a beat using a bucket, a ruler and the dining hall bell."

replies.npc: It's genuinely good. The juniors start dancing in the corridor.
"Borrowed. Creatively."

convos.open: "I miss my friends back home. But I'd miss you lot more if I left."

replies.npc: "Don't make it weird." They are smiling.
"…The food is better. That's all I'm admitting."

convos.open: "Teach me how to eat eba properly. I've been doing it wrong for a year."

replies.npc: Roll, dent, dip, swallow. They nail it on the third try. You feel like a proud parent.
"I KNOW. That's why I'm asking!"

convos.open: "Junior! Come here. Have you eaten today?"

replies.npc: "Good. Show me your tummy. …Hmm, I'll allow it."
"Haba!" They push half a loaf into your hand. "Eat. Now."

convos.open: "Who's disturbing you? Give me names."

replies.npc: "Hmm. If somebody touch you, you know where I dey."
"Leave am for me." By evening, the bully apologises to you. Strangely politely.

convos.open: "WAEC is killing me. Quiz me on Biology. Anything."

replies.npc: They answer perfectly. Then cry a little. Then laugh. WAEC does things to people.
"Then learn it with me. Two birds."

convos.open: "My junior, you're doing well. Teachers are saying your name nicely."

replies.npc: "Don't thank me. Keep it up."
"I no go tell you. Make your head no swell."

convos.open: "When I graduate, who will look after you?"

replies.npc: "Correct answer. But you can still write to me."
"Ah ah. Don't cry, you'll make me cry." Too late.

convos.open: "Junior. Why are you walking like you own this corridor?"

replies.npc: "Hmm. Walk properly." They let you go.
"Just walking?" They stare. You hold their stare. They let you go first.

convos.open: "Bring your Strongman. Inspection."

replies.npc: "Small? You think I be small pikin?" They take it anyway.
"Finished. Hmm." They search your box. It's not finished. Bad day.
A shocked silence. "…What did you say?" Frog jumps follow. But people saw.

convos.open: "My father was in the army. He trained me like a soldier. That's why."

replies.npc: They look at you like nobody has ever said that. Then: "Go to your class."
"…No. It isn't." They say nothing else.

convos.open: "You're new. What's the hardest part so far?"

replies.npc: "It gets lighter. Not easier — lighter. You'll see."
They laugh. "The beans never get easier."

convos.open: "A good leader listens more than they talk. Remember that."

replies.npc: "I believe you will." It sticks.
"Especially then. That's where the truth hides."

convos.open: "Senior, how do you fold a mattress so the house master doesn't shout?"

replies.npc: You show them the hospital corner. They practise it six times. Perfect.
"Then why do we fold it?!" Ah, the eternal question.

convos.open: "Senior, somebody took my provisions. I didn't want to tell you."

replies.npc: They whisper a name. You "have a word". The provisions return by evening.
They try to refuse. They fail. "Thank you, Senior."

convos.open: "Senior, were you scared when you were in JSS1?"

replies.npc: "Really?" They look so relieved. "Okay. Then I'm normal."
"Wow." They believe you completely. You feel a tiny bit guilty.

convos.open: "I came third in my class!"

replies.npc: They're practically bouncing. You buy them a Jolly Roll.
"Yes, Senior!" They salute. You did not ask for a salute.

convos.open: "Senior, I can do Mr. Bassey's voice. Listen. 'SIT DOWN BEFORE I SIT YOU DOWN.'"

replies.npc: "Emeka taught me," he whispers. "He's my hero."
Ali freezes. Nobody is behind him. You both laugh.

convos.open: "Senior, can I sit with you at dinner? The JSS2s are mean."

replies.npc: He sits and tells you his whole life story, including the time he fought a goat.
He makes no noise for six seconds. Then the goat story.

convos.open: "Junior! Go and fetch me water. Two buckets. Run."

replies.npc: Two buckets, three trips, one aching back. "Hmm. Slow." No thank you.
"Prep? Who asked you?" They let it go — today.
Gasps. Frog jumps. But two JSS1s look at you like a hero.

convos.open: "Why are you looking at me? You want to fight?"

replies.npc: "Look down when I'm passing."
They step closer. You don't step back. They "remember something" and leave.

convos.open: "Junior, how much do you have? Show me your pocket."

replies.npc: They take it. "Tax."
They pat your pocket. Your ₦500 is in your sock. Victory.

convos.open: "In my JSS1, Seniors made us sleep on the floor. You people are enjoying."

replies.npc: "Better be grateful." They walk away, oddly satisfied.

replies.say: 🤔 "So you're doing it back to us?"
replies.npc: "…Get out of my sight." It landed somewhere.

convos.open: "Junior… that tin looks heavy. Let me help you carry the Strongman."

replies.npc: They take four spoons. "One spoon," they say, licking the spoon.
You run. They don't chase. Too much effort.

convos.open: "When last did your mummy visit? Asking for… research."

replies.npc: "Saturday. Okay. Noted." You feel like you just revealed a state secret.
"Hmm. Pity." They lose interest immediately.

convos.open: "I'm starving, junior. Starving. Look at my face."

replies.npc: "God bless you." They actually mean it. Mostly.
"Hmm. Two starving people. This school will kill us."

convos.open: "Relax, junior. You look like somebody owes you money."

replies.npc: "It is. One day you'll miss it. Weird, right?"
"Ah. Then that face is correct."

convos.open: "You play draughts? Sit. Let me teach you a trick."

replies.npc: They teach you a sneaky double jump. You beat three classmates with it that week.
"No wahala. The board isn't going anywhere."

convos.open: "Don't mind those wicked seniors. Most of them were scared JSS1s too."

replies.npc: "I cried every night for a month. Don't tell anybody."
"Because nobody stopped them. Maybe you'll be the one."

convos.open: "Your portion of grass is still standing. Explain."

replies.npc: "Good. I like a junior with initiative." You suffer with initiative.
"Then sharpen it with your determination."

convos.open: "Saturday labour. Who wants the toilets and who wants the field?"

replies.npc: Smart choice. The toilet team returns looking haunted.
"Brave. I respect it." You earn a tiny bit of legend.

convos.open: "Junior, where is your table? Why are you at this table?"

replies.npc: "Good. Order is order."

replies.say: 🙏 "My friend is sad, I'm keeping her company"
replies.npc: The prefect hesitates. "…Five minutes."

convos.open: "Extra meat? Who told you there's extra meat?"

replies.npc: "Exactly. Nobody." You both know there's extra meat.

replies.say: 😇 "Senior, you look tired. I can help serve"
replies.npc: They narrow their eyes. Then hand you the ladle. You eat well tonight.

convos.open: "Junior. You were in the front row at assembly. Good. Stay there."

replies.npc: "Leaders are seen. Let them see you."

replies.say: 😅 "I was late, that was the only space"
replies.npc: The head prefect almost laughs. "Then be late in the right direction."

convos.open: "Inter-house is coming. Our house hasn't won in four years. FOUR."

replies.npc: "That's the spirit! 5 AM training."
"A cheerleader! We need noise!"

convos.open: "My junior! How's the bed? Anybody stealing your things?"

replies.npc: "Fine? Show me your locker." It is not fine. They fix it.
"Disappeared? Buckets don't walk." By evening, it walks back.

convos.open: "Junior, what's your name again?"

replies.npc: "{me}. Okay. I'll remember." You hope that's good.
A pause. Then a laugh. "You get mouth."

convos.open: "Go to the tuck shop and buy me Jolly Roll. Here's ₦200. Keep the change."

replies.npc: The change is ₦0. You knew. They knew. Still, a favour is a favour.
"Fine. Next time, no excuse."

convos.open: "You people in JSS1 are too free. In our time, we greeted every senior. EVERY."

replies.npc: "Better." They stride off happily.

replies.say: 😐 "Good afternoon, Senior. In our time too."
replies.npc: "…Is that sarcasm?" "No, Senior." It was.

convos.open: "Which house are you in, junior?"

replies.npc: "{house}? Ah. Best house. Or worst. Depends."
"You forgot your HOUSE?" Ten frog jumps to help you remember.

convos.open: "Junior, come and help me iron. My uniform is a disgrace."

replies.npc: You iron for twenty minutes. They give you a sweet. Fair trade.
"Then learn on my shirt!" You burn a small mark. You run.

convos.open: "Do you know how to make garri with sugar and groundnut properly?"

replies.npc: "A professional!" They let you make theirs. It's an honour. Sort of.
Shocked silence. "Who raised you?"

convos.open: "Junior, any gist? What are JSS1s saying about us?"

replies.npc: "Nothing? Hmm. Clever junior."
They look delighted. "Good. Very good."

convos.open: "Your shoes are dirty. Polish them before assembly."

replies.npc: Spotless. The VP compliments you. The senior takes credit.
"Then polish the rain." You don't know what that means. You polish anyway.

convos.open: "Your name is on the noisemakers list. Twice. Explain."

replies.npc: "…One time. Next time, no mercy." They cross it out with a sigh.
"You were laughing. Laughing is loud talking."
"Bribery? Of the class captain?" They take it. One name disappears.

convos.open: "The teacher left me in charge. Please. PLEASE be quiet."

replies.npc: The class goes quiet for six whole minutes. The captain looks at you like you're a miracle.
"I KNOW." They look like they might cry.

convos.open: "Can you help me collect the assignment books? Half the class is pretending to be busy."

replies.npc: You collect 31 books in ten minutes. You are now feared.
"I knew it."

convos.open: "Being captain is like being a goalkeeper. Nobody remembers your saves, only your mistakes."

replies.npc: They smile, surprised. "Thank you, {me}."
"Nobody else raised their hand."

convos.open: "Class party fund. ₦200 each. You're the last one."

replies.npc: "Thank you! Finally a responsible citizen."
"Next week is the party." They write 'owing' next to your name.

convos.open: "Exam season special: highlighters, ₦100. Glow in the dark, guaranteed."

replies.npc: It does not glow in the dark. It barely glows in the light.
"…The light is too bright here." You both know.

convos.open: "I'm running a lottery. ₦50 a ticket. Prize is a whole tin of Strongman."

replies.npc: You don't win. Nobody seems to win. The tin is never seen again.
"…My cousin. Pure coincidence."

convos.open: "You get anything to sell? I go find buyer for you. 20% commission."

replies.npc: Sold in an hour. You get ₦300. They get ₦75. Everybody wins.
"Everybody get something. Think am."

convos.open: "Abeg lend me ₦100. Business don jam bad market."

replies.npc: They return ₦150 two days later. "Interest. I be honest businessperson."
"Hmm. Okay. When you get, remember me."

convos.open: "Nice padlock. Very… strong. Where did you buy it?"

replies.npc: "Very strong, okay." They look disappointed in a suspicious way.
"Just admiring. I admire padlocks." They leave quickly.

convos.open: "I was just passing. I didn't touch anything. Why are you looking at me like that?"

replies.npc: "Is this your locker? Wow. I didn't know." They know.
They pass. Slowly. Looking at your locker.

convos.open: "Honestly, I don't steal. Things just… find me."

replies.npc: "I've tried." They seem almost sincere.
"…I will return the spirit of the biscuits."

convos.open: "Does my hair look okay? Be honest."

replies.npc: "I knew it, but thank you."
They fix it in your window's reflection. "Thank you. You're a real one."

convos.open: "Somebody slipped a love letter in my bag. With terrible spelling."

replies.npc: You recognise it instantly. You say nothing. Some secrets protect the innocent.
"'You are my sunshin.' No E." You both cry laughing.

convos.open: "Everyone thinks being fine is easy. I can't even eat beans in peace."

replies.npc: They do. They laugh loudly. Nobody stares — much.
"Exactly. A tragedy."

convos.open: "Social night is Saturday. What are you wearing?"

replies.npc: "Classic. Confident. I respect it."
"Fashion icon. Bold."

convos.open: "…" They nod at you and keep reading.

replies.npc: Forty minutes of comfortable silence. As you leave, they quietly say "thanks".
"Physics. For fun." They show you. It is not fun. They are very happy.

convos.open: "Can I ask you something? How do you make friends so easily?"

replies.npc: "Nonsense." They nod, like it's a formula. "I'll try."
"Good. Then it's not a skill I'm failing at." They smile.

convos.open: "I noticed you struggled with question four. It's simpler than it looks."

replies.npc: They explain it in three sentences. It makes total sense.
"Then let's start with one." Patient. Kind. Terrifyingly smart.

convos.open: "People think I'm proud. I just don't know what to say."

replies.npc: A tiny smile. "Okay. Anything. Noted."
"…Thank you."

convos.open: "Why did the JSS1 boy carry a ladder to class? Because he heard the exam was HIGH school!"

replies.npc: "THANK YOU. Tough crowd today, but you get it."
"…You're right. It was bad. I'll workshop it."

convos.open: "I did the principal's walk in front of the principal. He laughed. Then he gave me labour."

replies.npc: "Every minute. Every blade of grass."
"Brave or stupid. Same thing in this school."

convos.open: "I need a sidekick for my skit. You get the face for it."

replies.npc: "The face of someone who just got punished." It's a hit.
"Stage fright is just applause you haven't heard yet." Deep.

convos.open: "Shift. You're sitting in my favourite spot."

replies.npc: "Good." They sit. They don't thank you. Of course.
"…It is now." You don't move. They sit somewhere else, muttering.

convos.open: "Your Strongman. Small. Just one spoon."

replies.npc: It's three spoons. It's always three spoons.
"Brave." They walk off. You exhale.

convos.open: "I repeated JSS1, you know. Everybody laughs about it."

replies.npc: They look at you for a long moment. "…Okay." Something softens.
"Say that again." You don't.

convos.open: "Why is everyone scared of me? I'm nice. Sometimes."

replies.npc: "…More times." They seem to be calculating.
"Borrowed!" They return it. Huh.

convos.open: "Ehen! Have you heard? Gist of the century!"

replies.npc: You hear about a love letter, a ghost and a teacher's wig. Possibly the same story.
"You don't? …Then you won't mind hearing that people are talking about YOU." Now you do.

convos.open: "Somebody in SS2 is dating somebody in SS3 and the house master KNOWS."

replies.npc: They tell you. You wish they hadn't. You'll never look at Senior {sen} the same way.
"Boring. But fine." They go tell someone else.

convos.open: "Tell me something about you that nobody knows. I won't tell anybody."

replies.npc: "Smart. Very smart." They respect you a little more.
"MONSTER." By dinner, the whole class knows.

convos.open: "They say {mate} cried in the toilet yesterday. You know why?"

replies.npc: "…Oh. Yes. Maybe." They look a bit ashamed.
"I'll find out." They always do.

convos.open: "Let's pray before the test. Join hands."

replies.npc: The prayer is long and includes your future children. You feel strangely calm.
"God hears hearts too. But louder is faster."

convos.open: "Bible study tonight. Snacks provided. Real snacks."

replies.say: 🍪 "I'm there for the Word… and snacks"
replies.npc: "Honesty is a virtue!" They save you the biggest biscuit.
"Prep is also holy if done with faith."

convos.open: "I fasted today. I am weak. Distract me from the smell of the dining hall."

replies.npc: You tell the whole plot of a Nollywood film. They make it to sunset.
"Get behind me, Satan." They say it lovingly.

convos.open: "Race to the dining hall? First one gets the big meat."

replies.npc: You lose. The meat is gone. They give you half. Sport.
"Dignity gets the small meat."

convos.open: "I trained at 5 AM. Tomorrow you're coming. No excuses."

replies.npc: They do. You regret everything. But you run 400m without stopping.
"Your bed is your enemy."

convos.open: "The ball burst. Again. Who has ₦500 for a new one?"

replies.npc: "Hero!" You're now an honorary team member.
They actually do. It goes badly for the mango.

convos.open: "I saw you come back late from the tap. I'm not saying anything. Yet."

replies.npc: "I saw nothing." Bribery works. Sadly.
"Hmm." They write something in the air with their finger.

replies.say: 🤝 "We're classmates. Let's look out for each other"
replies.npc: They blink. Nobody has ever said that to them. "…Okay. Maybe."

convos.open: "The house master asked me who was talking after lights out. I didn't say your name."

replies.npc: "You owe me." They're smiling, but it's a real smile this time.
"…Somebody who deserved it." Chilling.

convos.open: "Everybody hates me because I tell the truth."

replies.npc: "…Is there a difference?" They really don't know.
They look at you, startled. "Not everybody?" "Not me."

convos.open: "Which subject you hate pass?"

replies.npc: "Maths hates you back. It's mutual."
"Agric na labour with extra steps."
"Liar. Who hurt you?"

convos.open: "If you get ₦10,000 now, wetin you go do?"

replies.npc: "Correct answer. No notes."
"And the house master go buy am from you for free."
"Ehn? You be old man?"

convos.open: "I dreamt that the school burnt down. I woke up happy, then sad, then happy again."

replies.npc: "Because they'd just build another one."
"I already rebuked it. Twice."

convos.open: "Garri with sugar or garri with groundnut?"

replies.npc: "A person of culture."
"Your teeth go file report."
"Rich person garri. I see you."

convos.open: "Who do you think will be head prefect when we reach SS3?"

replies.npc: "Then I'm your vice. Give me position now."
"Hmm. Maybe. They're loud enough."

convos.open: "Do you think teachers have feelings?"

replies.npc: "Mr. Bassey definitely doesn't."
"Deep. Very deep."

convos.open: "My bucket handle broke. I'm carrying water like a baby now."

replies.npc: "You're an angel. A bucket angel."
"Engineering!" It holds for exactly one day.

convos.open: "Can I tell you something? I don't like Agege bread."

replies.npc: "I KNOW. I've been hiding it for a year."
"Finally. A safe space."

convos.open: "I want to be a pilot. Everybody laughs."

replies.npc: "Thank you. First class seat for you, free."
"Destination: home. Departure: now."

convos.open: "You get extra biro? Mine don die for middle of note."

replies.npc: "I go return am." They will not. Biros never come back.
"Then we share. You write one line, I write one line."

convos.open: "I'm writing a letter to my crush. Help me with big English."

replies.say: ✍🏾 "'Your beauty is more than the sum of its parts'"
replies.npc: "Wow. Is that maths or love?" "Both."
"Too direct! Are you mad?"

convos.open: "Our dormitory smells like feet and determination."

replies.npc: "80% feet, 20% determination."
"Revolutionary." They actually join you.

convos.open: "Do you think the ghost in the old lab is real?"

replies.npc: "STOP. Don't tell me that before I sleep."
"Then go there at midnight." You don't.

convos.open: "I miss my mum's jollof so much I dreamt about it."

replies.npc: They describe it in such detail you both get hungry and sad.
"Don't insult my mother like that."

convos.open: "If you could change one rule in this school, what would it be?"

replies.npc: "Then nobody would read. Good rule, bad idea."
"You should be principal."
"Revolution starts in the dining hall."

convos.open: "Can you keep a secret? I failed the test. My parents can't know."

replies.npc: "Thank you. I'll study harder." They mean it.
"Seriously? Thank you." You meet after prep for a week.

convos.open: "What's the first thing you'll do when vacation starts?"

replies.npc: "Same. Wake me in January."
"Eat for me too."
"Cartoons or Nollywood?" "YES."

convos.open: "I think the Maths teacher likes me. He only shouted at me twice today."

replies.npc: "I knew it. True love."
"…Oh no."

convos.open: "You know how to play Ayo? Teach me abeg."

replies.npc: Twenty minutes later they beat you. You regret everything.
"Deal. Bring seeds."

convos.open: "Somebody stole my socks. Both of them. Who steals SOCKS?"

replies.npc: "Desperate people with cold feet."
You find them on the fence. Nobody knows how. Mystery solved, mostly.

convos.open: "I'm tired of beans. My stomach has started a protest."

replies.npc: "My stomach is ON STRIKE."
"You just saved a life." It's a biscuit, but okay.

convos.open: "Why is the dining hall rice always half-done?"

replies.npc: "Al what? Speak English."
"Educational rice."

convos.open: "Have you finished the assignment? I just need to… see your format."

replies.npc: They "check the format" for 20 minutes. Your answers are now their answers.
"Selfish. But fair."
You both finish. Theirs is actually better.

convos.open: "How many days left till Visiting Day?"

replies.npc: "Every day here is three days."
"My big aunty. She brings the biggest cooler." Your stomach notes this.

convos.open: "Do you ever feel like the bell is following you?"

replies.npc: "Rising bell, class bell, dinner bell, ghost bell."
"Ding ding. Wake up. Ding ding. Sleep."

convos.open: "What's your house cheer? Teach me, I keep forgetting."

replies.npc: You both shout it in the corridor. A senior shouts back. Worth it.
"Then we're both traitors. Silent traitors."

convos.open: "I want to change my seat. My seatmate eats chalk."

replies.npc: "Like biscuit. Calmly. Every day."
"Can I? You're the best."

convos.open: "Our class is the best class in the whole school. Agree or disagree?"

replies.npc: "Correct. The other arms are jealous."
"Same thing."

convos.open: "I learned how to wash my own shirt properly. My mum would be shocked."

replies.npc: "Thank you. It only took one semester."
"Define clean."

convos.open: "Do you think we'll remember any of this when we're old?"

replies.npc: "Even the beans?" "Especially the beans."
"So all of it, then."

convos.open: "My uncle says boarding school builds character. My character is crying."

replies.npc: "Under construction for six years."
"You promise?" "I promise." You hope you're right.

convos.open: "Tell me a joke. I need one today."

replies.npc: They laugh. A real one. "Thank you, I needed that."
"Just… home stuff. A joke is enough." You tell one. It helps.

convos.open: "Who's your best teacher?"

replies.npc: "Really? Interesting choice."
"Free period. The best teacher of all."

convos.open: "I think I left my slippers at the tap. If anybody wears them, I'll know."

replies.npc: You find them on a JSS2 boy's feet. He pretends not to understand English.
"I did. In capital letters. Somebody crossed it out."

convos.open: "Is it normal to miss your siblings even though they annoyed you every day?"

replies.npc: "I even miss my little brother's noise. Strange."
"What's that?" "Missing your kidnappers."

convos.open: "Let's make a pact: whoever gets rich first buys the other one a car."

replies.npc: You shake hands seriously. Somewhere in the future, a car waits.
"Fine. Bicycle, then car."

convos.open: "Which senior do you fear the most?"

replies.npc: "Same. Everyone does. Even teachers."
"Brave words for someone who ran from a lizard yesterday."

convos.open: "Can I copy your Agric note? I was 'sick' that day."

replies.npc: "You're a lifesaver." They return it with a doodle of a cow on page 3.
"…Sleeping is a type of sick."

convos.open: "Somebody said I look like the Chemistry teacher. Do I?"

replies.npc: "I'm changing schools."
"Thank you. I needed that."

convos.open: "Do you think the principal ever went to boarding school?"

replies.npc: "Trauma. Generational trauma."
"In a suit. With a cane."

convos.open: "I made a calendar to count days till vacation. I'm crossing out hours now."

replies.npc: It is very detailed. It has hours. It has minutes. It's concerning.
"…How many good days?" "Let's make some."

convos.open: "I found a lizard in my shoe. We're roommates now."

replies.npc: "Gerald." Gerald moves out the next morning. Sad.
"And walk barefoot to class? Never."

convos.open: "This rain no go stop. Our shoes don turn swimming pool."

replies.npc: You run. You both slip. You both laugh in the mud.
"Real friend!" You arrive half-dry. That counts.

convos.open: "Rain means no labour today. Thank God."

replies.npc: "Let it rain till Monday."
"Why would you say that out loud?"

convos.open: "My lips are cracking like dry ground. This harmattan is wicked."

replies.npc: "You're a blessing." Your shea butter is now community property.
"Thank you. I've been practising."

convos.open: "The dust is in my nose, my ears, my soul."

replies.npc: "Fashion and function."
"A dusty one."

convos.open: "This heat is not normal. I'm melting like ice block."

replies.npc: "Life saver. Literally."
You sit in the shade for ten minutes. Bliss.

convos.open: "NEPA again! How will I read in the dark?"

replies.npc: You both read with one torch. Very close. Very hot. Very studious.
"God has spoken. Amen."

convos.open: "No light, no fan. My bed is a frying pan."

replies.npc: "With the cockroaches? No thank you."
"You're now my best friend."

convos.open: "Exam starts tomorrow and I haven't read anything. Anything."

replies.npc: You read for three hours. It helps. A little.
"Sleep is also studying. Brain needs rest."

convos.open: "If I fail this exam, my dad will make me sell bread on holiday."

replies.npc: You quiz each other at dinner. They know more than they thought.
"Not funny!" It's a little funny.

convos.open: "Do you think the exam questions are the same as last year's?"

replies.npc: "WHAT. Why didn't anybody tell me?" Off they run.
"I wasn't! …Okay I was."

convos.open: "Test today. I wrote formulas on my palm. It's sweating off."

replies.say: 🧼 "Wash it off before you get caught"
replies.npc: "…You're right." They wash it. They pass anyway.
"Betrayed by my own hand."

convos.open: "It's Visiting Day! Who's coming for you?"

replies.npc: "Save me some chicken. Please. Begging."
"Then come with me. My mum brings food for twenty."

convos.open: "My parents didn't come. I'm fine. Totally fine."

replies.npc: They try not to cry. They eat two plates.
"Yeah. Next time." They don't sound sure.

convos.open: "You look hungry. You're walking like a zombie."

replies.npc: They laugh and give you half their bread.
"Three hours is three years in hunger time."

convos.open: "Your face is telling me you didn't sleep."

replies.npc: "The holy trinity of boarding school."
"Your eyes are not fine. Take a nap in siesta."

convos.open: "I heard you got punished. Your knees okay?"

replies.npc: "Rest in peace, knees."
"It never is. Same here."

convos.open: "Why do you look so down today?"

replies.npc: "Me too. Sit with me at dinner."
"If you're not okay, I'm here." They mean it.

convos.open: "Bro/sis, you need a bath. With love."

replies.npc: "Flies are filing complaints."
"Eau de Boarding House."

convos.open: "Saturday! No class! Let's do something mad."

replies.npc: The whole set plays until the house master blows a whistle at you.
You win two rounds. They demand a rematch. Forever.

convos.open: "Sunday afternoon and nothing to do. This is what boredom feels like."

replies.npc: You both write. They write three pages. To their dog.
"Wise words."

convos.open: "Night has come and my mind is on home."

replies.npc: They tell you about their little sister's cartoon obsession. You both smile in the dark.
"Fair point. Goodnight."

convos.open: "You're broke too? Welcome to the club. Membership is free, obviously."

replies.npc: "Exactly."
"Like what?" "Ideas." They laugh. Then actually consider it.

convos.open: "You came top five?! Teach me your ways, sensei."

replies.npc: "Every day? That's a lot of days."
"Proud. Very proud." They're laughing.

convos.open: "Your result wasn't great, eh? Mine either. We're a team."

replies.npc: "Team Next Term! We'll rise like bread."
"They'll be upset, then they'll help. That's parents."

convos.open: "SS1 and we're finally not the smallest. How does it feel?"

replies.npc: "Don't let it get to your head."
"Strange is right. Who are we now?"

convos.open: "Science, Arts or Commercial — did you choose right?"

replies.npc: "Confidence! I envy you."
"Wise."

convos.open: "The juniors call me 'Senior' and I keep looking behind me."

replies.npc: "I'm not ready for this responsibility."
"I will. I remember being them."

convos.open: "WAEC registration fees. My dad sighed for eleven minutes."

replies.npc: "I had nothing else to do."
"Biggest year of our lives, they say."

convos.open: "JAMB, WAEC, NECO. Three exams, one brain. Not enough brain."

replies.npc: "Group brain. Like ants."
"Yes. Seriously, yes."

convos.open: "After graduation, what's your plan?"

replies.npc: "Simple. Clean. I like it."
"A gap year of sleep."
"Osas has inspired a generation."

convos.open: "I can't believe we're in SS3. I still remember crying on resumption day."

replies.npc: "We've come so far."
"Shut up."

convos.open: "Will you sign my shirt first on sign-out day? Reserve the back."

replies.npc: "Deal. Write something deep."
"Obviously."

convos.open: "Being a senior is hard. Juniors don't listen, teachers don't trust you."

replies.npc: "You sound like the principal."
"Sandwich life."

convos.open: "I sent a junior to buy bread and he came back with a story instead."

replies.npc: "Something about a goat. I didn't ask. I just ate the story."
"I am a senior. This is my destiny." You both laugh.

convos.open: "My first love letter was in JSS2. It had a drawing of a heart. A very bad heart."

replies.npc: "I ate it." What.
"Embarrassing. But cute."

convos.open: "Prefect list is coming out. Do you want a post?"

replies.npc: "You'd be good."
"Smart."

convos.open: "Ah, {me}. Did you understand today's lesson? Honestly."

replies.npc: "Then explain the last point to me." You manage. Mostly.
"Thank you for honesty. Come to the staff room after class." Ten minutes, and it clicks.

convos.open: "Why were you yawning in my class? Was it boring?"

replies.npc: "Sleep is part of studying. Fix it." A rare kind tone.
"Good." They nod. Respect noted.

convos.open: "You're doing better this term. Keep it up."

replies.npc: "Don't thank me. Thank your effort."
"I can tell." They actually smile.

convos.open: "Where is your assignment? The one due today."

replies.npc: "Good. Neat handwriting, too."
"You don't have a dog. You live in a hostel." Fair point.
"First thing tomorrow. First."

convos.open: "When I was your age, I trekked five kilometres to school. Barefoot."

replies.npc: "Uphill. Both ways." They almost wink.
"Inspiring enough to do your homework?"

convos.open: "What do you want to be when you grow up?"

replies.npc: "Then Biology is your friend. Treat it nicely."
"Then argue less with me and more with your books."
"Famous for what? Think about it."

convos.open: "I see you've been helping your classmates. That's good character."

replies.npc: "Character lasts longer than results. Remember that."
"That's even better."

convos.open: "Your handwriting looks like a chicken walked through ink."

replies.npc: They laugh despite themselves. "Practise. One page a day."
"Good. Neatness shows respect."

convos.open: "Come here. Carry these books to the staff room for me."

replies.npc: "Thank you. You're a good student." A small gift: an old revision guide.
You carry them. Your arms complain. Your teacher remembers.

convos.open: "Some of you think teachers don't care. We care too much, that's the problem."

replies.npc: "Do you? Then prove it with your results."
"…Fair question. A question I ask myself." Huh.

convos.open: "Exams are coming. Are you ready?"

replies.npc: "Confidence is good. Preparation is better."
"Then start today. Come for extra lessons on Thursday."

convos.open: "You did very well in the test. I'm proud of you."

replies.npc: "Keep your head down and keep going."
"It shows."

convos.open: "Your result was disappointing. What happened?"

replies.npc: "Then prepare. You're smarter than this result."
Their face softens. "Come and talk to me if you need to."

convos.open: "In SS classes, nobody spoon-feeds you. You must read on your own."

replies.npc: "Good. The library is your second home now."
"…Teaspoon. That's all."

convos.open: "WAEC is not a monster. It is a test. Prepare and it will bow."

replies.npc: "That's the spirit."
"Then let's shrink it. One past question a day."

convos.open: "NEPA took the light. Class continues with your imagination."

replies.npc: "Neither did my school. Sit down."
"Excellent suggestion." The whole class plays quiz. Fun!

convos.open: "Young one. Do you know what our motto means?"

replies.npc: "Good. Now live it." He walks on, hands behind his back.
"Something about everything." A rare smile.

convos.open: "How is life in the hostel? Be honest. I won't punish honesty."

replies.npc: "I will speak with the bursar." A week later, a new tank arrives.
"Fine is not a report. But thank you."

convos.open: "I read your name in the honours list. Well done."

replies.npc: "Don't stop now."
"I don't make mistakes in honours lists." He means it.

convos.open: "Why are you outside during class hours?"

replies.npc: "Hmm. Quick quick."
"Which teacher?" You name one. She nods slowly.

convos.open: "Your uniform is neat today. That's how I like it."

replies.npc: "Keep it like that and we'll never quarrel."
"Creative. Not allowed. But creative."

convos.open: "Your continuous assessment is uneven. Strong here, weak there. Balance."

replies.npc: He points at two on the sheet. Very specific advice.
"Good. I'll be checking."

convos.open: "My pikin, your face is dry. You dey drink water?"

replies.npc: "Drink! Water is free. Medicine is not."
"Try harder. And eat your beans."

convos.open: "Who wet the bed in Room 4? I won't tell anybody. I just want to change the sheet."

replies.npc: "Good. Don't know loudly either."
"God bless you. Nobody will know." Kindness happens quietly here.

convos.open: "Provision inspection tomorrow. Make sure your box is neat."

replies.npc: "And no contraband. I can smell Kwik Noodles from my office."
"Anything you're hiding." Gulp.

convos.open: "You're here again? Is it malaria or Maths test?"

replies.npc: She checks your temperature. "Hmm. Small fever. Rest here one hour."
"At least you're honest. Go to class. Drink water first."

convos.open: "Wash your hands before you eat. Half this school's problems would disappear."

replies.npc: "Good. Tell your friends."
"With the water you're wasting on bucket fights."

convos.open: "Ehen! My pikin, you want extra rice? Carry this pot for me first."

replies.npc: It's heavy. Mama gives you a mountain of rice. Worth it.
"Late for food? Hmm. Next time."

convos.open: "The beans has weevils because the supplier is a thief. Not my fault!"

replies.npc: She laughs so hard she drops the ladle. "You this pikin!"
"At least somebody understand."

convos.open: "Who taught you to eat so fast? Slow down, food won't run."

replies.npc: "Hmm. That's survival, not manners." She gives you extra stew.
"No sorry. Just chew."

convos.open: "You want to buy something or you just dey window-shop?"

replies.npc: "Looking is free. Touching is ₦50."
"Fresh Jolly Roll. Hot. Like your future."

convos.open: "Somebody touch my shelf last night. If I catch am…"

replies.npc: She looks at you for a long time. "Hmm."
"Wicked! Thank you, my pikin."

convos.open: "Credit is finished. No credit. Don't even look at me with that face."

replies.npc: "…One Jolly Roll. ONE. Pay Friday."
"My best customer!"

convos.open: "Sannu. You don greet me today? Ehen, that's better."

replies.npc: "Allah ya kiyaye. Go well."
"The news is bad, the music is good. Like life."

convos.open: "Twenty years at this gate. I've seen boys become doctors and girls become judges."

replies.npc: "I already see it. Go and read."
"Every Christmas, one or two. They bring me kola. Good children."

convos.open: "WHO DEY THERE?! …Ah, na you. Why your eye dey open by this time?"

replies.npc: "Sit by the fire small. Then go sleep. Bingo, greet am."
"The toilet is that way. Not this way."

convos.open: "You hear that noise? From the old lab? …Na cat. Na cat."

replies.npc: "Scared? Me? …Walk me pass the lab." He is very scared.
"Definitely. A big cat. With white cloth."

convos.open: "Student, where you dey go this night?"

replies.npc: "Straight. No branch."
"Good evening. Go and sleep before I change my mind."

convos.open: "You're here voluntarily? Outside exam period? Remarkable."

replies.npc: "Then you have taste. Take this — the best novel nobody borrows."
"Silence is the best study partner."

convos.open: "This book was due two weeks ago."

replies.npc: "Late, but returned. That's more than most."
"Then renew it. Officially. Like a citizen."

convos.open: "Your fees are paid. Don't worry. Some children are not so lucky."

replies.npc: "Thank your parents."
"That's confidential." He looks at a long list and sighs.

convos.open: "You know which crop eats the most water? Rice. You know which eats the least? Excuses."

replies.npc: "Come on Saturday. I'll show you how to plant yam."
"Farmers are the first philosophers."

convos.open: "My pikin, please don't throw biscuit wrapper on the floor. Na me go pack am."

replies.npc: "God bless you. You get home training."
"Ah! Look at this one!" She tells everyone about the student who helped.

convos.open: "I know everybody's secret in this school. Everybody."

replies.npc: "Especially the principal's." She winks and keeps sweeping.
"Your secret is safe. You're one of the nice ones."

convos.open: "How is your spirit, my child?"

replies.npc: "Then rest in Him. And in your bed, early."
"Wonderful. Help someone whose spirit is weak."

convos.open: "Assalamu alaikum. Did you pray Asr today?"

replies.npc: "Alhamdulillah. Keep your prayers like your books."
"Late is better than never. Go now, there is still time."

convos.open: "I see everything in this hostel. Everything. Remember that."

replies.npc: "Good. Keep your corner clean and we'll be friends."
"…I did. Well done." Unexpected.

convos.open: "Noise after lights out last night. Who?"

replies.npc: "Hmm. Everybody was asleep. The noise was asleep too, I suppose."
"Thank you." Your dorm will find out. They always do.

convos.open: "Good afternoon, Senior! Please, how do I get my bucket back from the tap? A senior took it."

replies.npc: You walk over. The bucket is returned with an apology. The junior looks at you like a superhero.
"Thank you, Senior! I'll return it shining!" They do.

convos.open: "Senior, is it true that the old lab is haunted?"

replies.npc: Their eyes go wide. You feel a tiny bit guilty. Only a tiny bit.
"Oh thank God." They exhale for the first time in a week.

convos.open: "Senior, I don't understand fractions. Can you help me?"

replies.npc: Ten minutes with a mango cut into pieces. They get it. You feel like a teacher.
"Okay, Senior." They look disappointed.

convos.open: "Senior, my provisions are finished and Visiting Day is far."

replies.npc: "God bless you, Senior!" They tell the whole JSS1 class about you.
"Okay, Senior." They go off, hoping.

convos.open: "Senior, I want to be like you when I reach SS."

replies.npc: "Better? Is that possible?" Flattery works on you, apparently.
"Yes, Senior!" They actually start sweeping.

convos.open: "Senior, the bully in my class keeps taking my food."

replies.npc: You have a quiet word with the bully. It stops. Just like that.
"…Okay. I'll try." They look terrified and brave.

convos.open: "Senior, what's the secret to surviving here?"

replies.npc: They write it down. In their hand. Literally.
"Mama Iyabo?" "Mama Iyabo." Wisdom passed on.

convos.open: "Senior, please don't send me on errand, I have test tomorrow."

replies.npc: "Thank you, Senior!" They run off. You feel kind.
They go. They come back. They'll remember both.

convos.open: "Senior, are you scared of WAEC?"

replies.npc: "Senior is scared? Then I can be scared too." Strangely comforting.
"Wow." They believe you completely.

convos.open: "Senior, I miss my mummy. Is that normal?"

replies.say: 🫂 "Very normal. I cried for a month"
replies.npc: "A whole month? …Okay. Then I'm normal." They smile.
"Second term. Okay. I'll wait."

convos.open: "Senior, they said seniors used to make juniors drink garri without water. Is it true?"

replies.npc: "Did you?" "Never." They look relieved.

replies.say: 🙂 "Not in this hostel. Not while I'm here"
replies.npc: They tell everybody. JSS1s sleep better that night.

convos.open: "Senior, can I sit with you at dinner?"

replies.npc: They tell you about their first week. It's just like yours was.
"Okay, Senior." They try. It works. They make a friend.

convos.open: "Senior! I came first in a test! First!"

replies.npc: They're practically glowing.
"Yes, Senior!" Fire in their eyes.

convos.open: "Senior, how do I tell my parents I want to be a musician?"

replies.say: 🎸 "Show them your grades first, then your music"
replies.npc: "Grades first, then music. Okay." They nod seriously.
"…Honestly. Scary. Okay."

convos.open: "Senior, somebody is spreading rumours about me."

replies.npc: You casually defend them in front of the right people. The rumour dies by dinner.
"Really?" "Really." It takes a week, but it dies.

convos.open: "You're in SS now. Feel the pressure yet?"

replies.npc: "Wait till SS3. Pressure plus pressure."
"Spoken like someone who hasn't seen WAEC."

convos.open: "Our set is leaving soon. Take care of this school."

replies.npc: "I know you will. You were a good junior."
"Ah, don't cry. I'll come and visit."

convos.open: "Let me give you one advice about SS3: start reading NOW."

replies.npc: "Good. I started too late. Don't be me."
"Yesterday."

convos.open: "Ehen! You. You get extra water? The tap don dry."

replies.npc: "You don save my life." You're now somebody's hero.
"We go die together."

convos.open: "Did you hear the generator scream this morning? I thought it was a goat."

replies.npc: "…Was it?" You'll never tell.
"It needs prayers."

convos.open: "Have you seen my slippers? Blue. Left one has a name."

replies.npc: Found under the mango tree. Nobody knows why. Nobody ever knows why.
"Slipper thieves. Organised crime."

convos.open: "Your house won the cheering competition. Congratulations, I guess."

replies.npc: They laugh. Rivalry, but friendly.
"LOUDER. But the judges were blind."

convos.open: "Which mango tree has the sweetest mangoes? I'm asking for science."

replies.npc: "A person of knowledge. Thank you."
"Fair. Mango secrets are sacred."

convos.open: "I lost my ID card. If the VP asks, I'm invisible."

replies.npc: "Shhh. Nobody can see us talking."
"There's a lost and found?!" Off they go.

convos.open: "The dining prefect gave me the smallest fish in the history of fish."

replies.npc: "I needed a magnifying glass."
"You're a saint."

convos.open: "This school has more rules than Lagos has traffic."

replies.npc: "Exactly!"
"No running in the corridor. What if there's a fire?!"

convos.open: "Somebody painted a smiley face on the principal's car. With toothpaste."

replies.npc: "Nobody knows. Legend says it was a JSS3. Or a ghost."
"Toothpaste Picasso."

convos.open: "Do you think they'll ever fix the borehole?"

replies.npc: "God and the bursar. Both are slow."
"Our children will enjoy it."

convos.open: "Ten-ten after siesta? I'm the champion of my class."

replies.npc: You lose spectacularly. Their footwork is witchcraft.
"Coward." They're smiling.

convos.open: "I heard you're good at Maths. Is that true?"

replies.npc: "Then help me with simultaneous equations. You have five minutes."
"Humble. Suspicious."

convos.open: "Somebody is selling suya behind the fence at night. Have you tried it?"

replies.npc: "Very real. Very spicy. Very illegal." You decide to forget this conversation.
"Baba Sunday is scared of the dark." Brave words.

convos.open: "Okay, honest question: are boarding school friends forever friends?"

replies.npc: "Then let's be the best ones."
"Some is enough."

convos.open: "You're my person, you know that? Since day one."

replies.npc: "Since the crying night." They bump your shoulder.
"We BOTH cried."

convos.open: "Somebody said you talk about me behind my back. I don't believe it. Just… tell me it's not true."

replies.npc: "I knew it." The relief on their face is huge.
"One small thing is still a thing." They walk off. It takes two days to fix.

convos.open: "You told my secret. I don't know if we can go back."

replies.npc: "…I need time." It's not a no.
The silence says everything.

convos.open: "You're the only person who doesn't make me feel like a robot."

replies.npc: "Robots don't cry during Maths. I checked."
They actually laugh. Loudly. People turn.

convos.open: "I read your essay. It was… good. Better than mine in one paragraph."

replies.npc: "Don't make it weird. It was ONE paragraph."
"The third. I'm stealing your metaphor."

convos.open: "You taught me to read. You know what that means? Everything."

replies.npc: "We did the work." They mean it.
"Forever."

convos.open: "Still angry about the bucket thing? Long time now."

replies.npc: "Water inside the bucket." They grin.
"…I'll pay. With interest."

convos.open: "You laughed at my worst joke yesterday. That's loyalty."

replies.say: 😂 "It was so bad it was good"
replies.npc: "That's my brand."
"And that's why you're in my thank-you speech."

convos.open: "You took the punishment with me for the blackboard. Nobody does that."

replies.npc: "Team Kneeling. The best team."
"Mine too. They send greetings."

convos.open: "If I ever build a school, you're teaching there."

replies.npc: "Whatever you're best at. Kindness, maybe."
"Fine. You can blow the whistle."

convos.open: "You know what my mama said? 'Any friend that stops you from wrong is a real friend.'"

replies.npc: "Wisest woman in Benin."
"Who else?"

convos.open: "You reported me in JSS1. I still remember."

replies.npc: "…Okay. Business is business, sorry is sorry."
"Allegedly." He shrugs.

convos.open: "You returned my notebook without reading it. I still think about that."

replies.npc: "It was mine." She smiles. "Thank you."
"…Which page?" Panic. You're joking. Probably.

convos.open: "Remember that Visiting Day? You saved me."

replies.npc: "I don't know if I would have, then. I would now."
"Tell her I said thank you. Again."

convos.open: "Remember the contribution? I still have the list of everyone who gave."

replies.npc: "So I never forget who I owe."
"I owe everybody. That's what makes me work."

convos.open: "You bought me boots. I'll never forget that."

replies.npc: "Every goal. Every single one."
"Double. Triple."

convos.open: "You were the first person I told about my brother."

replies.npc: "I know. That's why I told you."
"Better. He writes poems now. Sad ones, but poems."

convos.open: "You said my drawings were good. I've drawn every day since."

replies.npc: Today's drawing: the hostel at sunset. There are two tiny people on the balcony.
"I will. For me. And a little for you."

convos.open: "You ran my campaign. I owe you my whole political career."

replies.npc: "Minister of Snacks."
"We did the work."

convos.open: "You were the first person to move your bag for me. Do you remember?"

replies.npc: "I remember everything about that day. The good and the bad."
"Best for me too."

convos.open: "Junior, I hear you're doing well. I'm proud of you."

replies.npc: "I told you. Be better than the wicked ones."
"Flattery! I taught you that too."

convos.open: "Can I tell you my plan to escape Saturday labour?"

replies.npc: The plan involves a fake sprained ankle and a cardboard crutch. It's doomed.
"Not this one." It fails.

convos.open: "Our house master snores during prep. Everybody knows."

replies.npc: "Like TWO generators fighting."
"He can't hear. He's snoring."

convos.open: "The new JSS1s look so small. Were we that small?"

replies.npc: "And louder."
"Rude." They laugh.

convos.open: "What's the worst punishment you've ever had?"

replies.say: 🌾 "Cutting grass with a cutlass for 3 hours"
replies.npc: "Amateur. I had to count the leaves on the mango tree."
"Your thighs must be strong now."

convos.open: "I swapped my Jolly Roll for two biscuits and a story. Good trade?"

replies.npc: "A senior fell in the gutter during inspection. Worth every crumb."
"You weren't there. The story was amazing."

convos.open: "Do you ever practise your signature for when you're famous?"

replies.npc: You both practise on the back of your notebooks. Yours has a star. Theirs has two.
"Show me. …The fourth one is criminal."

convos.open: "If this school were a Nollywood film, what would it be called?"

replies.npc: "I'd watch it."
"Too real."
"Award-winning."

convos.open: "I think my slippers have a ghost. They move at night."

replies.npc: "…That explains so much."
"Same, slippers. Same."

convos.open: "Teach me one word in your language."

replies.npc: They practise it all day. They thank everyone, in your language. Adorable.
They use it on a senior. You both run.

convos.open: "What do you think happens to the food the dining hall throws away?"

replies.npc: "The goats eat better than us."
"STOP."

convos.open: "Want to start a study group? Just us and two others."

replies.npc: The study group meets twice, then becomes a gossip group. Still useful.
"Ours will." It doesn't. But it was nice.

convos.open: "I bet you can't name every teacher in the school."

replies.npc: You get 28 out of 33. They are deeply impressed.
They get 11. You both laugh.

convos.open: "I'm trying to stop saying 'omo'. It's been two hours."

replies.npc: "Omo, it's hard." They realise immediately.
"My mum says it's not proper." "Omo, your mum."

convos.open: "Who's the best dancer in our set?"

replies.npc: "Prove it on Social Night."
"Yes! Their legs are not legal."

convos.open: "My family is moving to Abuja. I might change schools."

replies.npc: "I don't want to. I'm begging my dad."
"Every month. Promise."

convos.open: "Somebody put sugar in the salt container in the dining hall."

replies.npc: "The beans was SWEET. Disturbing."
"Nobody knows. Everybody suspects Emeka."

convos.open: "Do you ever wonder what our teachers were like as students?"

replies.npc: "Definitely. Class captain. Noisemakers list."
"With chalk in hand."

convos.open: "I keep forgetting my locker combination. It's my own birthday."

replies.npc: "Pressure."
"Then everyone knows my birthday." "Then everyone buys you a present." Genius.

convos.open: "Is it just me, or does Monday morning assembly last for three years?"

replies.npc: "And the principal says 'finally' four times."
"They'd take the chair AND me."

convos.open: "I want to be the first in my family to go to university."

replies.npc: "Say it again. I need it."
"Seriously? Thank you!"

convos.open: "Sometimes I just sit by the tap and watch people. It's like TV."

replies.npc: "Yesterday a senior slipped and pretended he meant to."
You watch for ten minutes. It's better than TV.

convos.open: "Did you know crickets can tell the temperature?"

replies.npc: "Since always. Count chirps in 14 seconds, add 40. Fahrenheit."
"Crickets don't do Maths. But they do Physics."

convos.open: "If you could have one superpower here, what would it be?"

replies.npc: "Strategic. I respect it."
"Hero of the people."
"Boring. But useful."

convos.open: "Our corridor smells like Kwik Noodles. Somebody has a heater."

replies.npc: "Hmm. Your eyes are shining."
You follow it. It leads to a prefect's room. You both leave quietly.

convos.open: "I'm going to write a book about this school one day."

replies.npc: "As a hero or a villain?" "Surprise me."
"'Garri at Midnight'."

convos.open: "Swap: my Strongman for your groundnuts?"

replies.npc: Excellent trade. You both win. Economics.
"Selfish. But I understand."

convos.open: "The fan in our class makes a noise like it's crying."

replies.npc: "Same, fan. Same."
You poke it with a ruler. It stops crying. It also stops working.

convos.open: "Do you believe in luck?"

replies.npc: "Boring. Correct, but boring."
"Double protection."

convos.open: "Rising bell at 5 AM is a human rights violation."

replies.npc: "Already drafting the letter."
"I see it with my eyes closed."

convos.open: "Morning duty again. Who designed this roster? I want names."

replies.npc: You finish in record time. The house master looks suspicious.
"Cursed by the labour prefect."

convos.open: "Bath time and the queue is longer than the WAEC syllabus."
